candidate.answerReason: The quadratic terms cancel, leaving -3x+2x=-x. Substituting x=5 gives -5.

methods.label: Expand and combine
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 8 monomial-by-polynomial multiplication and Grade 7 polynomial addition and subtraction.

methods.label: Factor out x
methods.explanation:
Both terms have a factor \(x\), so factor it out to simplify one bracket:
\[
x(2x-3)-2x(x-1)=x\bigl[(2x-3)-2(x-1)\bigr].
\]
The bracket equals \(2x-3-2x+2=-1\). Thus the expression is \(-x\), and when \(x=5\), its value is \(-5\).
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 8 common-factor extraction followed by Grade 7 removal of parentheses and combining like terms, at the same maximum level as the main method.

candidate.annotationRationale:
Simplifying and then evaluating is the route-neutral target. The retained route expands products and combines polynomials. The alternative extracts the common factor x, then removes parentheses and combines like terms inside the bracket. Numerical substitution is shared support. Factoring is an optional route, not an additional task requirement.
